title: DML statements, Database methods, partial success, save results, and transaction control
objectives: Choose a DML statement versus a Database class method for insert, update, upsert, delete, undelete, or merge.
Explain allOrNone false as partial success and how to read Database.SaveResult.
State that DML statements throw on bulk failure while Database methods can return per-row results instead.
Place savepoints and rollback as transaction-control neighbors without replacing APEX-010.
diagnostic_question: A sandbox loader must insert 200 LAB_Stop__c rows and keep the good ones if ten fail validation. Would you write insert stops; or Database.insert(stops, false), and what would you read on each SaveResult?
definition: DML writes sObjects to the Salesforce database. Apex offers DML statements (insert, update, upsert, delete, undelete, merge) that throw on error, and Database class methods that can allow partial success and return SaveResult (or sibling result) arrays. Transaction-control methods such as setSavepoint and rollback live on Database as well. ([DML Statements vs. Database Class Methods](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/langCon_apex_dml_database.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers listen for allOrNone, SaveResult.isSuccess, and the fact that one list DML is one statement. Choosing insert when you needed partial success rolls back the whole batch; choosing Database.insert(list, false) without inspecting results silently drops rows.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a bank teller versus nightly settlement. A DML statement is the teller window: if one check in the stack bounces, the whole stack stops and an exception is thrown. Database.insert(list, false) is settlement: each slip gets a SaveResult—paid or rejected—with errors you must read. convertLead and some recycle-bin APIs exist only on Database. Savepoints are the audit stamp you can roll back to; APEX-010 owns the deep concurrency story.
deeper_explanation: Use DML statements when any error should throw and interrupt control flow (try/catch). Use Database methods when a bulk operation should allow remaining rows to succeed; pass false as the optional allOrNone parameter (default true). ([DML Statements vs. Database Class Methods](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/langCon_apex_dml_database.htm))

Database.insert/update return SaveResult arrays aligned with the input list. Inspect isSuccess, getId, and getErrors. convertLead is only a Database method. Database also exposes transaction control, emptying the Recycle Bin, and query helpers. ([SaveResult Class](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexref.meta/apexref/apex_methods_system_database_saveresult.htm))

Partial-success bulk DML from SOAP defaults or allOrNone false can retry a subset up to three attempts; triggers refire on the successful subset; governor limits reset between those attempts. A third-attempt failure surfaces a documented batch-retry error. ([Bulk DML Exception Handling](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_dml_bulk_exceptions.htm))

List DML counts as one DML statement, not one per row—cite 150 statements and 10,000 DML rows from Execution Governors and Limits (APEX-007). Do not mix certain setup objects with non-setup DML in one transaction. Deep savepoint/locking design is APEX-010.

mental_model.analogy: A bank teller window versus nightly settlement with per-slip rejection notices.
useful_mapping: DML statement insert list → teller: one bounce stops the whole stack and throws
Database.insert(list, false) → settlement: remaining slips can still post
SaveResult → the paid/rejected notice for one slip
allOrNone true (default) → treat Database like the teller
convertLead → a back-office operation that has no teller-window verb
setSavepoint/rollback → an audit stamp you can rewind to (APEX-010)
where_it_breaks: Partial success is not 'ignore errors'; you must read SaveResult.
Triggers still fire and share governors on retry subsets.
Setup-object mixing is a hard platform rule, not a teller preference.
The analogy does not encode order of execution (APEX-009).

teach_back_prompt: Explain DML statements versus Database.insert(list, false) to a teammate using the teller-versus-settlement idea, then name one place that analogy breaks.

Two-minute interview: partial success versus savepoint rollback.

  Write --> Db[Database class method]

flowchart TD
  Need[Need DML?] --> Q1{Must remaining rows succeed if one fails?}
  Q1 -->|No fail the unit| Stmt[DML statement or Database allOrNone true]
  Q1 -->|Yes keep good rows| Part[Database.insert list false]
  Part --> Read[Read every SaveResult]
  Need --> Q2{Lead convert or savepoint?}

claims.claim: DML statements throw Apex exceptions on bulk errors. Database methods can pass allOrNone false so remaining rows may succeed and return a result array instead of throwing.

Some setup sObjects cannot be mixed with non-setup DML in the same transaction. Database also provides transaction-control APIs.

Per-row success or error from a Database method.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: DML statements throw on error. Database.insert(list, false) allows partial success and returns SaveResult you must inspect. convertLead and savepoints are Database-only. List DML is one statement.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I start from the business rule: must one bad row fail the batch? If yes, insert list or Database with allOrNone true. If a loader should keep good LAB_ rows, Database.insert(list, false) and loop SaveResult. I mention three-attempt partial-save and trigger refire so they hear I read Bulk DML Exception Handling. I do not mix User-role DML with Account in one transaction. Savepoints are APEX-010.

terminology.plain: The Apex verbs insert, update, upsert, delete, undelete, and merge.
terminology.precise: Standalone DML that processes sObjects and throws a DmlException when a bulk error should interrupt control flow.
terminology.example: insert new List<Account>{ new Account(Name='LAB_A'), new Account(Name='LAB_B') };
terminology.confusable_neighbor: SOQL SELECT, which reads and is not DML.
terminology.boundary: merge and undelete have extra rules; convertLead is not a statement.

terminology.plain: Database.insert/update/delete and related APIs that can return results.
terminology.precise: Class methods that perform DML with an optional allOrNone flag, plus operations that have no statement form (convertLead, some recycle-bin and transaction APIs).
terminology.non_example: A SOQL Database.query call—that is not DML.

terminology.plain: Keeping the rows that saved when others failed.
terminology.precise: Database DML with allOrNone false (or SOAP default partial save). Failed rows are reported; remaining rows can succeed. Triggers may refire on retry subsets.
terminology.example: Loader keeps 190 good LAB_Stop__c inserts when 10 fail validation.
terminology.non_example: Catching DmlException after insert list and assuming the good rows committed.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Savepoint rollback of the whole unit (APEX-010).
terminology.boundary: You must inspect results; partial success is not silent ignore.

terminology.plain: The per-row outcome of Database insert or update.
terminology.precise: Array aligned with the input sObjects. isSuccess, getId, getErrors. Sibling types exist for delete and undelete.
terminology.non_example: A debug log line with no result object.
terminology.boundary: getId null behavior on some failed updates is version-sensitive.

terminology.plain: The flag that says fail all rows or allow partial success.
terminology.precise: Optional Boolean on Database DML. Default true: one failure throws and remaining rows do not proceed. False: result array, partial success possible.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Trigger addError on one row in a bulk trigger—related but not this flag.
terminology.boundary: Statements have no allOrNone parameter; they throw.

terminology.plain: Savepoints and rollback on the Database class.
terminology.precise: Database.setSavepoint and rollback let you rewind DML inside one Apex transaction. Mixed DML and locking details continue in APEX-010.
terminology.example: Savepoint sp = Database.setSavepoint(); try { insert a; } catch (DmlException e) { Database.rollback(sp); }
terminology.non_example: allOrNone false, which is per-call partial success, not a named savepoint.
terminology.boundary: This lesson only introduces the APIs; concurrency is later.

when_to_use: When an Apex class must write records and you need to choose DML statements versus Database methods.
When partial success is required and SaveResult (or delete/undelete results) must be inspected.
When convertLead, emptyRecycleBin, or savepoint APIs force a Database method rather than a DML verb.
When explaining transaction control at a high level before the deeper APEX-010 locking lesson.
when_not_to_use: Do not use DML statements when the loader must keep valid rows after some validation failures—use Database methods with allOrNone false.
Do not treat SaveResult as optional logging; unread results hide lost rows.
Do not mix setup-object DML with Account-style DML in one transaction.
Do not use this DML lesson as a SOQL/SOSL primer (APEX-003/004) or as a full savepoint/locking design (APEX-010).
configuration_or_code_location: Apex class or anonymous Apex in a disposable sandbox.
Debug logs: DML_BEGIN / DML_END statement counts.
Developer Console for DmlException versus SaveResult errors.
Setup only for verifying validation rules that cause expected failures.

worked_example.scenario: A sandbox loader inserts LAB_Stop__c rows for a shipment. Ten rows omit a required field on purpose. The good rows must remain. A second method converts a LAB_ Lead and must use the correct API. No production data.
inputs: List of 20 LAB_Stop__c, 10 missing required fields
One Lead eligible for convert in the sandbox

decisions.because: Partial success is required; a DML statement would throw and keep nothing.
decisions.rejected: insert stops; inside try/catch hoping good rows committed

decisions.decision: Read getErrors on failures; do not retry blindly in the same list without fixing data.
decisions.because: Partial success still reports why a row failed.
convertLead is only a Database method.
decisions.rejected: A convert DML statement that does not exist

configuration_or_code: for (Integer i = 0; i < results.size(); i++) { if (!results[i].isSuccess()) { System.debug(stops[i].Name + ' ' + results[i].getErrors()); } }
worked_example.output: Ten LAB_Stop__c rows exist; ten failures are visible on SaveResult; lead convert uses Database.
verification: SOQL count of LAB_Stop__c is 10, not 0 and not 20.
Debug shows REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING or equivalent on failures.
insert stops; in a scratch copy rolls back all 20—contrast documented.
worked_example.self_explanation: Partial success needed Database methods and unread SaveResult would have hidden the ten failures.

hands_on_lab.environment: Disposable sandbox; Account or LAB_ custom object with a required field.
starting_state_checks: A validation rule or required field can fail on purpose.
steps: Build a list of two Accounts: one valid LAB_Good, one missing Name.
Run insert list in try/catch and record whether either row exists.
Run Database.insert(list, false) and print each SaveResult.
Write one sentence on convertLead existing only as a Database method.
guided_completion: If both rows exist after the throwing insert, the missing-Name case did not fail as expected.
If you skip looping SaveResult, redo that step.
hands_on_lab.independent_challenge: Add Database.update(list, false) on a mix of valid and stale Ids; compare getId notes for your API version.
evidence: SaveResult debug for the failed row.
stop_recovery_cleanup: Do not deploy the loader to production.
hands_on_lab.limitations: Does not prove mixed DML with UserRole or three-attempt SOAP retries.

decision_table.signal: Any failure should abort the Apex unit and roll back that DML call's work.
decision_table.choose: DML statement or Database method with allOrNone true (default).
decision_table.not: Database.insert(list, false) without caring about results.
decision_table.why: Statements and default Database methods throw and interrupt control flow.

decision_table.signal: A loader must keep valid rows when some fail validation.
decision_table.not: insert list; plus an empty catch.
decision_table.why: Partial success is the documented allOrNone false behavior.

decision_table.signal: You need to convert a Lead in Apex.
decision_table.why: The guide states convertLead is only a Database class method.

decision_table.signal: You updated a UserRole and an Account in one method and got mixed DML.
decision_table.choose: Split setup and non-setup DML across transactions.
decision_table.why: More About DML documents the setup/non-setup mixing restriction.

limitations: Does not list every DML governor number except by citing APEX-007 / Execution Governors.
Savepoint isolation and FOR UPDATE locking are APEX-010.
Order of execution around DML is APEX-009.
Mixed DML object lists are release-sensitive.
security_notes: Partial success can leave an org half-updated; design compensating actions.
Do not log SaveResult messages that contain customer PII.
common_mistakes: Assuming try/catch around insert list commits the good rows.
Looking for a convert DML statement.

troubleshooting.symptom: DmlException: first error on row 0; no rows in the database.
check: You used a DML statement or allOrNone true.
Fix data or switch to partial success if that is the product rule.
troubleshooting.do_not_assume: SaveResult was returned; statements throw instead.

troubleshooting.symptom: Some rows missing after Database.insert(list, false).
check: Validation, FLS, or duplicates on those rows.
troubleshooting.do_not_assume: The platform dropped rows at random.

troubleshooting.symptom: Mixed DML exception mentioning setup objects.
check: User, UserRole, Group, and similar setup DML in the same transaction as Account-style DML.
Move one side to async or a later request.

production_notes: Bulk list DML; never DML in a loop.
Treat unread SaveResult as a production defect.
No production deployment is authorized by this lesson.

mcqs.prompt: What is the default allOrNone behavior on Database.insert?

options.A: True: one failure throws and remaining sObjects are not processed
options.B: False: partial success is the default

mcqs.rationale: The optional parameter defaults to true, matching throwing DML-statement behavior.

distractor_explanations.B: False must be passed explicitly for partial success.
distractor_explanations.C: The parameter exists on Database methods.

mcqs.prompt: When should you prefer a DML statement according to the guide?

options.A: When any bulk error should throw and interrupt control flow
options.C: When you must keep successful rows after failures

mcqs.rationale: Use DML statements if you want errors thrown as Apex exceptions.

options.A: A SaveResult array aligned with the input list
options.B: Always a thrown DmlException and no array

mcqs.rationale: SaveResult arrays correspond positionally to the sObject list.

mcqs.prompt: Which operation is only a Database method, not a DML statement?
mcqs.rationale: The guide states convertLead is only available as a Database class method.

mcqs.prompt: On partial-success retries, what happens to triggers?

options.A: They fire on the first attempt and refire on subsequent successful subsets

mcqs.rationale: Bulk DML Exception Handling says triggers fire on the first attempt and refire on subsets.

distractor_explanations.C: This is still pre-commit DML work.

mcqs.prompt: Which SaveResult method reports whether that row saved?
mcqs.rationale: isSuccess returns true if the DML operation succeeded for that object.

mcqs.prompt: insert accounts; in a for-loop of 200 rows is wrong because?

options.A: Each insert is a separate DML statement toward the per-transaction cap

mcqs.rationale: List DML counts as one statement; per-row DML burns the statement governor (150 cited on the limits page / APEX-007).

distractor_explanations.C: Statements throw; they do not return SaveResult.

mcqs.prompt: You DML a UserRole and an Account in one method. What documented issue can occur?

options.A: Mixed DML: setup and non-setup sObjects cannot share one transaction

mcqs.rationale: More About DML documents the setup/non-setup mixing restriction.

mcqs.prompt: Where do savepoints live in the Apex API?
mcqs.rationale: Database provides transaction-control methods; this lesson introduces them and defers depth to APEX-010.

mcqs.prompt: During second and third partial-save attempts, governors do what?

options.A: Reset to their original state before the first attempt

mcqs.rationale: Bulk DML Exception Handling states governors reset between those attempts.

mcqs.prompt: Which statement separates a DML Apex class from business data?

options.A: Deploying the class does not insert Account rows; DML at runtime does
options.B: SaveResult objects are custom objects in Setup

mcqs.rationale: The class is metadata. Inserted rows are data.

mcqs.prompt: You catch DmlException after insert list. Did the successful-looking rows before the failure commit?

options.A: No. An exception rolls back processed DML in that transaction unless you used a documented partial-save path
options.B: Yes, always, because Apex commits per row

mcqs.rationale: Throwing DML is all-or-none for that operation; exceptions roll back processed DML. Partial success requires the Database false path.

distractor_explanations.B: Apex does not commit each row independently on a throwing insert.
distractor_explanations.D: Trigger timing does not change statement semantics.

flashcards.back: insert, update, upsert, delete, undelete, and merge.

flashcards.back: Partial success, convertLead, recycle-bin helpers, or transaction-control APIs.
True: one failure throws; remaining rows are not processed.
No. Triggers fire and can refire on retry subsets.

flashcards.back: Up to three documented attempts; then a batch-retry error can fail the operation.

flashcards.back: Anti-pattern. One list DML is one statement.

flashcards.front: Account plus UserRole in one transaction?
flashcards.back: Mixed DML risk. Split setup and non-setup writes.
Database.setSavepoint and rollback; deeper design is APEX-010.

flashcards.back: No. Throwing DML rolls back that work. Use allOrNone false instead.
Failed rows disappear without an exception. Always inspect.

interview_questions.question: DML statements versus Database methods—how do you choose?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Statements throw and stop the bulk operation. Database methods can pass allOrNone false for partial success and return SaveResult. convertLead is Database-only.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I map the product rule first. Atomic fail-all: insert list. Keep good rows: Database.insert(list, false) and inspect results. I mention default allOrNone true so they hear I did not assume partial success. I keep savepoints as a pointer to APEX-010 and governors to APEX-007.
interview_questions.example: Loader uses Database.insert(stops, false); a payment class uses insert invoiceLines;
tradeoffs: Exception control flow vs result arrays

interview_questions.question: How do you read SaveResult correctly?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The array lines up with the input list. isSuccess, getId, getErrors. Never ignore the array after allOrNone false.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I loop by index so I can pair results[i] with rows[i]. I collect errors for a retry file. I mention getId version notes if they ask about failed updates. I do not treat a missing exception as success.
interview_questions.example: for (Integer i = 0; i < sr.size(); i++) if (!sr[i].isSuccess()) log(rows[i], sr[i].getErrors());
tradeoffs: Per-row retry vs failing the job

interview_questions.question: A catch around insert list shows a DmlException. The caller thinks the first 50 rows saved. What do you say?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: They did not. Throwing DML rolls back that work. If they needed partial success they must use Database.insert(list, false).
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I distinguish exception rollback from partial-save retries. I would not add a savepoint here unless they need a manual rewind (APEX-010). I would also check whether they DML'd in a loop, which is a separate governor defect.
interview_questions.example: insert stops; throws on row 51; SOQL count is 0, not 50.
follow_ups: What if the catch only logs and rethrows?
What about addError in a trigger?

interview_questions.question: Walk partial-success retry behavior.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The engine tries all rows, sets failures aside, retries the rest, and can try a third time. Triggers refire on subsets. Governors reset between attempts.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I cite Bulk DML Exception Handling. I warn that trigger logic must be idempotent because the subset can change. A third-attempt failure can surface the documented too-many-batch-retries message. This is not the same as my own for-loop retry.
interview_questions.example: SOAP API insert of 200 Accounts with 5 validation failures; triggers see 200 then 195.
tradeoffs: Idempotent triggers vs one-shot side effects
Partial success vs failing the API call
follow_ups: Does this apply to a simple insert statement from Apex?

interview_questions.question: When would you refuse partial success?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When the rows are one business document—invoice plus lines—and a half-write is worse than a throw.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Loaders and integrations often want allOrNone false. Financial postings usually want a statement or allOrNone true, sometimes with a savepoint around a larger unit (APEX-010). I also refuse per-row DML as a fake 'partial success' strategy.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Invoice__c plus lines uses insert lists in one transaction; a CSV account loader uses Database.insert(..., false).
follow_ups: How do you report skipped rows to an admin?
Where do you store SaveResult errors?
weak_answer_warnings: allOrNone false on every DML by habit

interview_questions.question: What is mixed DML, in one interview answer?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: You cannot DML certain setup objects with non-setup records in the same transaction because access levels would be inconsistent.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I give the classic UserRole plus Account example from the guide's idea. The fix is a separate transaction—often Queueable or a future, which is APEX-011. allOrNone false does not fix it. I mark the exact object list as needs verification against the current page.
interview_questions.example: insert account; then update UserRole in the same test method fails.
tradeoffs: Sync setup updates vs async split
follow_ups: Which objects are setup objects today?

interview_questions.question: Database.insert(list, false) 'succeeds' but rows are missing. Walk the diagnosis.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Read SaveResult. Failures do not throw. Check validation, duplicates, and FLS on the failed indexes.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I print results[i].getErrors() next to rows[i].Name. I confirm I did not also have a trigger addError. I check whether a later rollback (savepoint or uncaught exception) wiped the successes. I do not 'fix' it by switching to insert in a loop.
interview_questions.example: Ten LAB_ stops missing a required field; array has ten isSuccess false.
tradeoffs: Fail the job vs write an error file
follow_ups: How do duplicate rules appear on SaveResult?
What if getId is null on an update?
weak_answer_warnings: Assuming the method return means all rows saved

interview_questions.question: How is allOrNone false different from a savepoint rollback?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: allOrNone false is per Database call: some rows in that list can save. A savepoint rewinds the transaction to a named mark, including successful DML you already did.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I would use partial success for a loader. I would use a savepoint when a later step fails and the earlier insert must disappear—APEX-010. Mixing both without a diagram is how teams lose track of what committed. Interviewers want that vocabulary split.
interview_questions.example: Insert accounts with allOrNone false; later Database.rollback(sp) can still remove the successes if they were after the savepoint.
tradeoffs: One Database call vs multi-step unit of work
follow_ups: How many savepoints can you set? (Cite or mark needs verification.)
